5.	On April 25, 1874, Annie Jameson, a granddaughter of the founder of Jameson Irish Whiskey, gave birth to X in Bologna. X was a mediocre student who showed little academic promise and failed to get admission at the University of Bologna. Working in a makeshift laboratory in the attic of his family's country estate, he conducted experiments with a device that seemed to produce and detect a phenomenon first theorized by James Clerk Maxwell and demonstrated by Heinrich Hertz. X’s experiments sent signals first across a room, then across his garden, then across a hill. In 1901 he successfully transmitted a single Morse-code letter S (three dots) from Cornwall, England to St. John's, Newfoundland using a solid-state diode detector invented two years earlier by Y at the Presidency College in Kolkata without giving Y due credit. ID X (10 points) and Y (10 points). ‎<attached: 00126689-PHOTO-2026-04-25-08-47-35.jpg>
